name: Ba khia muoi
summary: Ba khía muối is a small mangrove crab, salted and eaten with hot rice. It feeds on fallen mắm fruit, so the meat is firm and the roe is scant.
origin: Rạch Gốc and the Ngọc Hiển mangrove. The 2024 culture-office listing puts Rạch Gốc at khóm 8, thị trấn Rạch Gốc, huyện Ngọc Hiển; later cape listings say xã Đất Mũi.
culture: The crabs gather in huge numbers around the tenth lunar month, which is why people salted them to keep them, as reported on 29 December 2019. Salting ba khía and the gác kèo ong honey trade were recognized together as national intangible heritage.
howToEat: Eat the salted crab with hot rice.
Phòng Văn hóa Thông tin huyện Ngọc Hiển also lists it steamed, stir-fried with tamarind, and grilled.
One commercial article describes pulling off the shell and mixing the crab with sugar, lime, garlic, chili, and rau răm.
where: Rạch Gốc and the Ngọc Hiển mangrove.
seoTitle: Ba khia muoi — salted mangrove crab
seoDescription: Ba khía muối from Rạch Gốc is salted mangrove crab with firm meat, eaten with hot rice. The crabs gather around the tenth lunar month.
